 Ford recalls 60,000 Transit vans over software glitch that shuts off lights

 Published  November 18, 2026 10:00 PM EST article Ford is recalling nearly 61,000 Transit vans over a software issue that could disable trailer lights, interior lighting and other electrical features. (Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 Ford is recalling nearly 61,000 Transit vans over a software issue that could disable trailer lights, interior lighting and other electrical features, according to federal regulators.
 Ford is recalling nearly 61,000 Transit vans over a software issue that could disable trailer lights, interior lighting and other electrical features, according to federal regulators.
 "A software error in the body control module C (BCMC) may cause the module to freeze, shutting off certain features such as interior lighting and trailer lights," the NHTSA said.
 A loss of trailer lighting could make the trailer harder for other drivers to see, increasing the risk of a crash .
 "If the trailer tail, position and reverse lamps do not illuminate, other drivers may have difficulty seeing the trailer, which can increase the risk of a crash," the recall notice reads.
 The recall was issued for 60,956 2026 Transit vans. (Jeff Kowalsky/Bloomberg via Getty Images  / Getty Images) 
 "The driver may receive multiple vehicle warnings indicating that the affected features are inoperative or operating in a degraded state," it added.
 Ford said it was not aware of any crashes or injuries related to the recall.
 The automaker estimates that all the recalled vehicles have the software glitch.

 Ford identified the problem while reviewing a warranty claim for an unresponsive control module in August. As of Oct. 2, the company said it had received 124 warranty claims, 53 field reports and one customer report in North America.
 Dealers will update the body control module software free of charge, or owners may receive an over-the-air update, which is expected to become available in January 2027.
 Owner notification letters were expected to be mailed beginning on Nov. 12, according to the recall notice.
